caption: The drawing depicts a formal garden plan viewed from above, with sections divided by wide tan paths and surrounded by rows of green trees and shrubs. The garden is split into multiple rectangular and geometrically shaped plots. At the top, a large rectangular section contains intricate, symmetrical flower beds in red, pink, and white, set within tan walking paths forming ornate curves and lines. Below this area is a narrower rectangular section with three smaller garden beds, two of which are diamond-shaped with pink, purple, red, and green plantings, and a central, rectangular bed filled with green specimens. Further down, there is a larger, square section with two oval garden beds filled with green and white plantings and surrounded by more colorful beds containing red, yellow, pink, and orange flowers. A circular fountain or structure is in the middle of this section, intersected by paths. At the bottom right of this section, a round compass rose is illustrated in tan and brown tones. The entire garden is enclosed by green lawns, with a wide, curved tan path entering from the lower edge and additional rows of varying-sized green trees and shrubs along the perimeter. The bottom of the image is labeled with the text: "THE A. C. RICHARDS GARDEN - THE BLACKWELL SURVEY 1860."
title: A. C. Richards' Garden
